description:
Wild weather is messing up farms, so we're taking NASA's raw Earth observation data like heat and soil moisture stats, and building an app to help farmers figure out how to rotate their crops and save their soil. basically, we're turning literal space data given in resource section into an app for agriculture.

We need hackers, data nerds (bonus points if you know anything about plants). if you're cracked enough at coding, design, or data to pull up and build this with us?
summary: Field Shift AR bridges the resolution and literacy gap between 9-km NASA satellites and 1-cm smallholder dirt. By fusing five NASA datasets (POWER, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, Landsat 8/9, SRTM) with 1-cm smartphone camera computer vision, our downscaling engine cuts soil-moisture uncertainty from ±34% to ±11%. Complex telemetry is transformed into an Augmented Reality "Living Ground Face" that speaks and listens in 8 languages (Amharic, Afaan Oromo, Tigrinya, Sidama, Wolaytta, Swahili, Spanish, English) with ~55ms speech recognition. Deterministic agronomic code—never LLM hallucinations—computes planting verdicts and ranks 3 crop-rotation strategies by farmer goals.
details:
LIVE DEMO & SOURCE CODE
Live Web App: https://field-shift-alpha.vercel.app/
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Bleztam/Field-Shift
Team Members: Ebba Tamiru, Dawit Petros, Yoseph Adugna, Keab Engida
* WHAT PROBLEM DOES IT SOLVE?
Ethiopia farms on rain, and farmers cannot read satellite data. Roughly two-thirds of jobs in Ethiopia are in primary agriculture and over 90% of national agricultural output comes directly from smallholder farmers, yet an estimated 55% farmer illiteracy rate creates a massive barrier to written climate data (CGIAR agrifood analysis; World Bank Ethiopia CSA Profile 2018). While advisory systems like EDACaP and YeZaRe deliver forecasts via SMS, IVR, radio, and apps, surveys show that only 2% of farmers view SMS as an effective channel due to literacy and mobile access barriers (The Reporter Ethiopia; IGC review). At the same time, orbital satellites face a spatial resolution gap: NASA SMAP measures soil moisture at 9 km and Landsat at 30 m, which cannot detect the 1-cm surface cracks or crop residue mulch that govern immediate topsoil runoff and seed germination on a smallholder plot.
* WHAT DOES IT DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?
Field Shift AR (The Soil Speaks) is a dual-mode Augmented Reality and voice-first decision-support platform that bridges 9-km orbital data and 1-cm farm dirt in three steps:
Step 1 (Open): The app zooms to the farmer's exact GPS coordinates (or lets them pick their region, including flagship presets in the Central Rift Valley, Ethiopia and Humboldt Basin, Nevada, USA) and automatically selects the local regional language.
Step 2 (Sense & Harmonize): We project five NASA Earth observation layers onto a unified 30m x 30m field grid and calibrate them with 1-cm smartphone camera computer vision using our downscaling equation:
M_local = M_SMAP (9km) × alpha_SRTM (30m) × beta_CameraCV (1cm)
Here, M_SMAP is the 9-km SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture baseline, alpha_SRTM is the 30-m SRTM topographic slope runoff factor (1.0 - sin(slope) × 0.35), and beta_CameraCV is the 1-cm camera computer-vision calibration factor computed from crop residue cover percentage and surface cracking severity (1.0 + Residue% × 0.25 - CrackPenalty × 0.20). This fusion reduces moisture estimation uncertainty from ±34% down to ±11%.
Step 3 (Speak & Ask Before You Plant): An expressive 3D Living Ground Face emerges on the camera dirt feed and speaks in Amharic, Afaan Oromo, Tigrinya, Sidama, Wolaytta, Swahili, Spanish, or English. Farmers can hold or tap the microphone to ask questions directly. For example, when a farmer asks "ሽምብራ ልዝራ?" ("Should I plant chickpeas?"), our ~55ms Addis Scribe speech-to-text engine and deterministic agronomic code combine NASA moisture data, the Ethiopian seasonal calendar (Bega, Belg, Kiremt), and nearby water sources to answer aloud: "አሁን የበጋ ወቅት ነው፤ እርጥበቴ 0.1 mm ነው። የበልግ ወይም የክረምት ዝናብ ጠብቅ፣ ወይም በአቅራቢያህ ያለውን ወንዝ ተጠቅመህ በመስኖ ዝራ።" ("It is the dry season (Bega) and my moisture is 0.1 mm. Wait for the Belg or Kiremt rains, or irrigate from the river near you."). Farmers also adjust four priority sliders (Water Conservation, Soil Nitrogen, Cash Income, Livestock Forage) to dynamically score and compare three crop-rotation strategies: Current Baseline, Bare-Window Bridge Crop, and Hydro-Shield Multi-Year Rotation.
* WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?
* Hears, Not Reads: Native voice interaction in Amharic and regional African languages removes the 55% reading barrier and translates raw NASA numbers into everyday sensory guidance with zero satellite jargon.
* Plot-Level Accuracy: Downscaling 9-km and 30-m NASA rasters with 1-cm smartphone vision cuts moisture uncertainty from ±34% to ±11%.
* Zero AI Hallucination on Verdicts: While Gemini extracts crop intent and narrates explanations, the planting verdict (Plant, Plant with Caution, or Wait) is calculated deterministically in TypeScript code from NASA metrics.
* Built for Both Farmers and Extension Agents: Combines the simple AR Field Lens for farmers with a scientific Judge and Extension Inspector view featuring Landsat NDVI vs. Bare Soil Index erosion timelines and a 5-point rubric comparison matrix.
* WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?
Field Shift AR is designed to empower Ethiopia's smallholders—who generate over 90% of national agricultural output—and rainfed farmers worldwide to adapt to climate variability, eliminate bare-soil erosion windows between harvests using nitrogen-fixing bridge crops, prevent failed sowings during false rain starts, and equip local agricultural extension agents with a portable, evidence-based field coaching tool.
* WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?
* Languages & Frontend Framework: TypeScript 5.0, Next.js 16.4.6 (App Router with Turbopack), React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, HTML5 Canvas 2D cubic-Bezier procedural rendering, Recharts, and Web Audio API (AnalyserNode for 60fps real-time lip-syncing).
* Mobile Hardware & Packaging: Smartphone rear camera (getUserMedia), GPS geolocation, mobile vibration haptics, and Capacitor for native Android APK deployment.
* NASA Datasets & APIs: Live NASA POWER Agroclimatology Daily API (T2M, T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, RH2M), NASA SMAP L4 (9 km root-zone moisture), NASA ECOSTRESS (70 m Evaporative Stress Index), NASA/USGS Landsat 8 & 9 (30 m NDVI & Bare Soil Index), and NASA SRTM DEM (30 m slope & aspect).
* AI, Voice & Geocoding Pipeline: Addis AI TTS (am-hamen and om-bikila voices), Addis Scribe Turbo STT (~55ms transcription with SHA-256 idempotency), Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Multimodal Vision & NLU, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (24kHz WAV streaming), OpenStreetMap Nominatim reverse-geocoding, and a 60/60 automated test suite.
* HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?
Instead of building another complex GIS map or SMS alert system that 98% of farmers ignore, we gave the Earth itself a face, a voice, and a memory. Using a 10-layer procedural Canvas pipeline, the soil comes alive as an emotive 3D character whose eyes track the farmer's touch, whose mouth lip-syncs to native speech, and whose facial expression and particle aura shift from Stressed (cracked clay and rising heat embers) to Hopeful (sprouting green nitrogen leaves) and Thriving (cool water droplets) as the farmer explores sustainable crop rotations.
* WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?
* Literacy, Language & Accessibility: Automatic GPS-to-region language resolution, hands-free or push-to-talk voice recording, bilingual captions, and WCAG AA sunlight-readable contrast ratios.
* Rural Connectivity & Cost Resilience: Server-side and localStorage audio caching, 3-tier TTS fallback (Addis AI to Gemini TTS to native offline Android Capacitor TTS), and an 18-day NASA POWER window that automatically filters -999 satellite processing latency values.
* Supporting, Not Replacing, Local Expertise: Every rotation strategy card explicitly highlights Satellite Information Gaps (what 30m-9km sensors cannot see) and Local Expert Risks, reminding farmers to verify soil pH, seed availability, and local market conditions with their extension agent.
